title: Define security patch SLA for Runtime LTS (qualification, turnaround, comms, verification)
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
We need an explicit, enterprise-grade SLA and process for security patches on the Runtime LTS line. Dedicated + Private customers are asking for (1) what counts as an LTS security patch, (2) response/turnaround expectations, (3) how we communicate advisories + patch availability, and (4) how we verify the patch and artifacts (including provenance/checksums/SBOM where applicable).

This ticket defines the SLA + workflow and produces a short policy write-up that can be referenced by Release Eng, SRE, Support/CS, and AEs. It should align with LTS backport policy and release gating, while providing a clearly documented out-of-band path for urgent security fixes.

Owners/partners
- Primary: Hanae Suzuki (vuln response coordination)
- Reviewers: Dr. Aisha Rahman (security policy sponsor), Connor O’Brien (Release Eng), Mateo Alvarez (Runtime), Sean Gallagher (SRE), Dev Patel (Support workflow)

Scope
- Define what qualifies as a “security patch” for LTS (including when it does NOT qualify for LTS)
- Define the severity rubric and expected turnaround times
- Define comms path (internal + external) and what we disclose
- Define verification steps and required sign-offs before publishing LTS artifacts

Out of scope
- Building the automation (tracked in ENG-4832 / ENG-4824)
- Rewriting the global security policy; this is LTS-specific operationalization

Proposed policy (draft)

1) Definitions: what qualifies as an LTS security patch
A change qualifies as an LTS security patch if it meets ALL of:
- Addresses a vulnerability that can impact confidentiality, integrity, or availability in production deployments of the serving runtime
- Affects at least one LTS-supported deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) OR a shared artifact used by those modes (runtime image, scheduler component, networking/auth sidecar shipped with runtime bundle)
- Has a clear reproduction path or credible upstream advisory (CVE, GHSA, vendor bulletin) indicating impact
- Can be implemented on the LTS branch with minimal diff and acceptable risk (per backport rubric)

Qualifying examples
- Remote crash / memory safety issue in runtime request parsing or KV cache code paths reachable via API inputs
- Privilege escalation or authz bypass in runtime admin endpoints (if present in the bundle)
- Container image base-layer CVEs above threshold where the runtime image is distributed to Dedicated/Private customers
- Supply chain issue in build/publish pipeline that compromises artifact integrity for LTS releases

Non-qualifying examples (generally handled via mainline + next scheduled LTS patch, or documented only)
- Low/medium severity CVEs in components not shipped to customers (build tooling only)
- Vulnerabilities that only affect non-LTS (experimental) features disabled on LTS
- Issues requiring large refactors or risky dependency upgrades on LTS without a safe backport path

2) Severity mapping and SLA targets
We will map to a simplified severity model (aligned with CVSS + exploitability) that is easy to communicate.

Severity levels
- Sev0 / Critical: Actively exploited in the wild OR unauthenticated RCE/priv-esc in a default LTS configuration, or a supply-chain compromise of shipped artifacts.
- Sev1 / High: High impact, plausible exploitation, no active exploitation observed; includes auth bypass, sensitive data exposure, or unauthenticated DoS with low complexity.
- Sev2 / Medium: Meaningful but constrained impact (requires auth, special config, or high complexity) with no known exploitation.
- Sev3 / Low: Low impact or defense-in-depth changes.

Turnaround targets (clock starts at internal confirmation of impact on LTS)
- Sev0 / Critical
  - Triage/confirmation: same business day (<= 8 hours)
  - Patch candidate ready (PR): <= 48 hours
  - Release artifacts + advisory: <= 72 hours
  - May be out-of-band (OOB) release outside monthly cadence
- Sev1 / High
  - Triage/confirmation: <= 1 business day
  - Patch candidate ready (PR): <= 5 business days
  - Release artifacts + advisory: <= 7 calendar days
  - OOB release allowed if customer risk warrants
- Sev2 / Medium
  - Patch in next scheduled LTS monthly patch OR <= 30 days, whichever comes first
  - No OOB unless escalated by Security + Runtime + SRE
- Sev3 / Low
  - Fold into next scheduled LTS patch; advisory optional (release notes mention)

SLA notes
- These are targets, not guarantees. If we miss targets, we must publish an internal postmortem note to #eng-releases and inform Support/CS of revised ETA.
- If a fix is not safely backportable, we must publish a mitigation/workaround (config, WAF guidance, feature disable) within the same SLA window.

3) Communication path (internal + external)
Internal comms
- Create a private tracking issue (Security internal) and link this Linear ticket + the LTS patch tracking PR.
- Notify:
  - #security-incident (triage + updates)
  - #eng-releases (release coordination)
  - #eng-sre (rollout monitoring readiness)
  - Support on-call + Support leadership (Dev Patel) for inbound ticket handling
- Release Eng assigns a Release Manager for the patch (typically Connor O’Brien or delegate).

External comms artifacts
- Security advisory (preferred): Redwood Security Advisory format with:
  - Summary, affected versions (LTS tags), severity, CVE/GHSA identifiers, mitigation, fixed versions, credit
  - Disclosure guidance (what we can/can’t share prior to customer upgrade)
- Release notes (required): LTS “Security” section entry with:
  - Identifier, severity, impact summary, upgrade action
  - Link to advisory if public; otherwise “Contact Support for details” for embargoed cases
- Customer notifications
  - Dedicated/Hosted: status page note only if customer-visible action required or elevated risk; otherwise email to account contacts for Dedicated (CS-managed)
  - Private: email to admin contacts with exact pinned versions + checksum verification instructions

Who sends what
- Support/CS sends customer-facing email using approved template (prepared by Security + Release Eng), with AEs looped for strategic accounts.
- Security owns advisory wording; Release Eng owns version strings, artifact URLs/checksums, and release notes.

4) Verification steps and required sign-offs (pre-publish)
Required verification for any LTS security patch
- Impact confirmation
  - Security confirms affected LTS versions and deployment modes
  - Runtime owner confirms reachability in default configs (or clearly documents required conditions)
- Code review + approvals
  - Minimum approvals: 1 Runtime approver + 1 Security approver (Dr. Aisha Rahman delegate) + Release Eng sign-off
  - If scheduler/kernel code touched: add Sofia Ivanova and/or Hiro Tanaka as required reviewers
- Testing gates (no waivers for Sev0/Sev1 without Security + SRE approval)
  - Unit/regression tests relevant to repro
  - Release-branch CI green (ENG-4824)
  - Scheduler smoke tests for release branches if applicable (ENG-4831)
  - Perf gates run + reviewed (ENG-4825); waivers must be documented with risk/rollback plan
- Artifact integrity + auditability
  - Artifacts built from tagged commit; provenance metadata attached
  - Checksums published; signing performed where supported (ENG-4832)
  - SBOM generated for the runtime image/bundle (or stub where not yet supported) with a link in the advisory/release notes
- Rollout readiness
  - SRE confirms monitoring/alerts are in place for LTS traffic and rollout (SLO dashboards) and that rollback path is documented
  - Dedicated/Hosted: staged rollout plan (canary then broad)
  - Private: clear “how to pin/rollback” steps with version strings

5) Emergency out-of-band (OOB) release procedure
Triggers
- Sev0 always triggers OOB unless Security explicitly approves waiting for scheduled patch.
- Sev1 may trigger OOB based on exploitability + customer exposure.

Process differences
- Shortened release window, but NOT reduced verification. Only allowable shortcuts:
  - Parallelize perf + CI; can ship if perf is within thresholds or SRE approves a temporary waiver with explicit rollback.
- Comms must be prepared before publish (Support/CS + advisory draft ready).

Deliverable
- Confluence page section under “Runtime LTS branch and backport policy” summarizing the above, plus a one-page Support/CS runbook excerpt.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Severity rubric + SLA targets approved by Security sponsor (Dr. Aisha Rahman) and Runtime exec sponsor (Mateo Alvarez)
- [ ] Comms path reviewed by Support workflow owner (Dev Patel) and CS lead (Rachel Kim) for pilot needs
- [ ] Verification checklist incorporated into the LTS patch runbook (ENG-4830) or linked as a required gate
- [ ] Publish final policy to Confluence and link from LTS docs (Release notes / LTS channel doc)

Open questions
- Should we set a hard CVSS threshold for base-image CVEs triggering OOB (e.g., >= 9.0), or use exploitability + customer environment?
- For embargoed vulns: do we always avoid public advisories until patch adoption crosses a threshold, or follow standard coordinated disclosure timelines?
comments: 2025-02-03 (Hanae Suzuki): Drafted severity levels + turnaround targets based on recent enterprise security review calls. Main open issue is how we handle base image CVEs vs runtime code CVEs; proposing CVSS>=9.0 + exploitable chain as the trigger, otherwise next monthly patch.

2025-02-05 (Dr. Aisha Rahman): Please add explicit language: SLA clock starts after internal confirmation that the vulnerability impacts an LTS-supported artifact/config. Also add requirement that any advisory must list affected/fixed versions even if details are limited under embargo ("limited disclosure").

2025-02-06 (Sean Gallagher): From SRE POV, no perf gate waivers for Sev0 unless rollback is immediate and canary shows stable p95. Add requirement: rollouts must be monitored via LTS-specific dashboards; if not available, release is blocked until SRE sets up temporary alerts.

2025-02-10 (Connor O'Brien): Added verification checklist items for provenance/checksums/SBOM and made Release Eng sign-off explicit. Once approved, I’ll incorporate into the patch runbook and the release manager checklist PR.

2025-02-12 (Dev Patel): Support needs a clear trigger for proactive outbound comms vs "respond on inbound." Suggest: Sev0/Sev1 always proactive for Private; Dedicated proactive if mitigation requires config change or immediate upgrade; Hosted only if customer action is required or there’s user-visible risk.

2025-02-18 (Mateo Alvarez): Looks good. Please clarify that fixes requiring large dependency upgrades on LTS are not guaranteed; we will provide mitigations if not backportable. Also call out that LTS will not accept feature-flagged security-hardening changes unless they directly reduce an identified vuln risk.
2025-02-19 (Hanae Suzuki): Updated draft accordingly and requested final approval from Aisha + Connor. Next: push text into Confluence under LTS change management + link from support playbook.
